correctness.rationale: For every S and T⊆S, the explicit allocation is efficient and its coalition slack is a sum of insertion-budget surpluses. If insertion inequality fails for U and b, the two-player restriction of an in-star has v({target})=F(U plus {b})>b+F(U)=v({source,target}), whereas v({source})=0; its core is empty. Under singleton normalization the complement worth identity v(N\{j})=v(N)−incoming(j) forces uniqueness. Standard multiset order-statistic zero-insertion and 1-Lipschitz properties verify the criterion for medians/quantiles. The independent code checker passed 6,228 exact-rational finite graph/operator cases; these are corroboration, not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The 2024 primary source proves nonempty core only for minimum-based trust games; the 2026 primary source proves their unique core and total balancedness and explicitly lists alternate external aggregators as a future direction. The new result is a necessary-and-sufficient universal insertion criterion with a converse empty-core star and nonminimum aggregators, not the known minimum case. Actual targeted mathematical-result searches returned no claim implying it. Publication-priority risk from nonindexed generic aggregator results remains.
residual_risks: Generic aggregation-function or cooperative-game theory outside the searched sources could contain an equivalent insertion-budget criterion.
The new theorem does not extend the minimum-specific unanimity or Shapley-complexity formulas.

value.rationale: The closest current paper proposes determining which mean, median and other external trust aggregation rules preserve stability. A necessary-and-sufficient criterion for universal total balancedness, a constructive core in every subgame, a sharp failure witness, and explicit validation for means, maxima and quantiles answer a structural question for whole families rather than a routine isolated instance. The criterion is directly usable for assessing alternative network reputation schemes without requiring power-index formulas.
